national.line: China set a Guinness World Record with 110 humanoid robots moving in sync. Finally, someone who can do the Cha Cha Slide on beat.
Cash-strapped friends surprised each other with gift cards so both could buy Grand Theft Auto 6. Now that's a gift swap nobody returns.
A San Francisco tech startup is paying $20 an hour to walk robot dogs for four to six hours. Easiest job ever: no treats, no bags, no barking.

The Who released "My Generation" 61 years ago, and Rolling Stone ranks it number 11 on its list of the 500 greatest songs. Pete Townshend reportedly wrote it on a train. Talk about a song that never got old.
A Nebraska woman got back the wedding ring she lost at a University of Nebraska-Lincoln football game, thanks to a friend and a news article. Turns out the newspaper still has some pull.
DoorDash is buying Instacart for $17 billion, joining two big delivery giants. Hope the tip is included.

pride.label: Life Saving Award
pride.line: Lebanon Fire Department gave its Life Saving Award on Oct. 26 to Tyler Blattel, Lt. Joe Gerber, Firefighters Adam Moppin, Nick Davis and Paul Shomo, Capt. Terry Saltzman, paramedic Louis Corbeil and EMT Jeremy Vinson for saving a Missouri Cooperage worker who collapsed from a cardiac event on July 8. Teamwork that kept a heart beating.

pride.label: Yellowjacket of the Week
pride.line: Ollie Sanders, a Lebanon High School colorguard member, was named Yellowjacket of the Week, and a favorite moment was winning best colorguard at Carthage. That's one student who knows how to flag down success.

pride.label: New Leader
pride.line: Lebanon Schools named Katie Cottongim its new Director of Communications. Yes, she'll be doing the talking.

pride.label: Navy Scholarship
pride.line: Chapel Banner, a Bolivar High School senior, earned a four-year Navy ROTC scholarship that covers full college tuition, one of about 100 chosen nationwide this year. Anchors aweigh, Bolivar.

pride.label: Apprenticeship Complete
pride.line: Julia Jones, a Bolivar High School graduate, finished her Dental Assistant Registered Apprenticeship through OCHC's Bolivar clinic and the BoMo Works program, and now plans to become a dental hygienist. Smile, she's earned it.

pride.label: District Champs
pride.line: Bolivar softball won the district championship by beating Aurora 12-2, then played in the state quarterfinal on Oct. 24. Those Liberators don't just swing, they win.

pride.label: World Champion
pride.line: Victoria Moroski, 17, of Lake of the Ozarks won gold in the under-18 women's skim division at the World Wakesurf Championships in Hangzhou, China, in October, and Team USA won gold too. She's officially riding the world's best wave.

pride.label: School Record
pride.line: Jacob Shurtz, a Fair Grove senior and two-time all-state pick, broke the school record for goals in a season by passing his older brother Andrew's 31. Sorry, big brother Andrew.

pride.label: Pro Bass Field
pride.line: Tyler Williams, a pro angler from Osage Beach, earned a spot in the 60-angler field for a $1.25 million bass tournament in Tennessee that runs Oct. 29-31. Hope the fish are feeling generous.

local.line: Level Up Lebanon wrapped its biggest season yet, with residents in Wards 1 and 4 hauling roughly 200 cars' worth of cleanup this fall. That's a lot of trunk space.

Camden County Public Water Supply District No. 5 got a $223,000 interest-free loan from the Missouri Department of Natural Resources to plan and design drinking water upgrades. Interest-free is everyone's favorite phrase.
Marshfield High School brought back its Marine Corps JROTC program after a four-year effort. Persistence finally earned its stripes.
Lake Regional Clinic in Osage Beach welcomes pediatric nurse practitioner Courtney Wood, who will provide acute walk-in care, well-child visits and sports physicals. Good news for scraped knees.

music.line: Cody Johnson says he used to drive to other towns just to fight cowboys before winning country music's biggest awards. Glad he found a better hobby.
Ella Langley became the fourth artist in country music history to score four number one hits in a single calendar year. She's running out of records to break.
Lainey Wilson will host the 60th CMA Awards solo, celebrating 60 years of country music. No co-host, no problem.
Zach Top added new arena dates to his Cold Beer & Country Music Tour. Time to start checking the calendar.
Morgan Wallen now curates his own 24/7 SiriusXM channel, Morgan Wallen Radio. Finally, a station that never skips a request.
Riley Green and Jon Pardi will headline Country Splash in Cabo alongside DIPLO. Sand in your boots instead of dirt.
Zac Brown Band, Russell Dickerson and Jo Dee Messina will play Daytona for Ford's first Veterans Day Classic. Start your engines and your guitars.
Lady A surprised fans with a new song, "Bigger Picture," that sets up their 10th studio album. Ten albums and still full of surprises.
Reba McEntire, Oprah Winfrey and Sabrina Carpenter joined ABC's celebration honoring Dolly Parton's life and legacy. Dolly would say the more the merrier.
Garth Brooks is releasing Double Live on vinyl for the first time on Nov. 6. Dust off the turntable.
Carrie Underwood headlines the 2027 Barefoot Country Music Festival lineup. Pack the flip-flops early.
Georgia football landed quarterback commit Bo Bryan, son of country star Luke Bryan. Dad's biggest hit may be his kid's arm.

weird.line: Texas firefighters brought out the Jaws of Life to free a raccoon with its head stuck in a tree. That raccoon will think twice before peeking.
A couple spotted a raccoon stuck in a dumpster in the cutest way possible. Dumpster diving has its risks.
A 3,156-pound jack-o'-lantern unveiled in Salem, Massachusetts, set a new world record. That's a lot of pie.
A 1,800-pound pop-up book just broke a world record. Don't drop it on your toe.
A channel catfish caught near Pittsburgh set a new record, topping the mark set in 1991. That one did not get away.
A deer found sitting alive in a car in Buffalo, New York, has gone viral. At least it picked the passenger seat.
A clumsy cow got a toy car stuck on its head. Somebody call roadside assistance.
A black bear shredded a car to pieces after getting locked inside. Bad review for the rental.
Ryan Ethridge grew a state champion pumpkin in Stephens County. That's one prize-winning patch.
A pet groomer YouTuber went viral after a goat turned out to be a "dream client." No tip needed, just snacks.
The Minnesota Zoo welcomed three orphaned brown bear cubs rescued in Alaska. Three new roommates, zero chores.
A Tennessee gymnast held a knuckle handstand for a record-breaking 1 minute, 23 seconds after more than four months of training. My wrists hurt just reading it.
A dinosaur fossil discovered in Montana sold for $47.3 million at auction. Somebody has a very expensive coffee table.
A Florida man blocked traffic to save a parking spot for his cousin. Family first, traffic second.
A Florida woman says a neighbor complained that her Halloween decorations were too scary. Mission accomplished, then.
A soccer match took a bizarre turn when the referee discovered the field was completely underwater. Nobody asked for water polo.
Mystery solved: the wrong-way driver reported in Waikele, Hawaii, was a work truck. Whoever blamed the truck owes it an apology.
Pumpkins nearly went extinct with the mastodons that spread their seeds until humans domesticated them. Thank goodness for pie.
Sea otters go "Pumpkin Dunkin'" in a zoo's adorable Halloween tradition. The pumpkins never stood a chance.
An angler says he caught the world-record striped bass during the eclipse of a full moon. Good timing, good fish.
A Missouri town is getting noticed for its hilarious water towers. Now that's some high-rise humor.

humor.line: The first message sent over ARPANET, the internet's ancestor, went out in 1969 and linked just four places: UCLA, Stanford, UC Santa Barbara and the University of Utah. Four computers back then, and zero cat videos.
Cats are America's most popular pet, with about 90 million house cats living here and over a third of households owning one. The cats insist they own the other two-thirds too.
Steel-cut oats are sliced with steel blades, while rolled oats are steamed and then rolled flat. One gets a haircut, the other gets a steamroller.
The first American doughnuts were little "nuts" of dough that Pilgrims brought to New England after learning to make them in Holland. Turns out the Pilgrims had a sweet tooth.
Breadsticks started in Turin, Italy, in the 1600s, and legend credits Antonio Brunero. Somebody finally figured out what to dip in the sauce.
Candy corn has a broad yellow end, an orange middle and a white tip, and it's made with sugar, corn syrup and confectioner's wax. Wax is a bold choice for candy.
It falls less than a week after National Pumpkin Day, so there may be a spare pumpkin on your counter. That pumpkin has run out of excuses.
Scientists think lemurs floated to Madagascar on vegetation from Africa's mainland, and much of the island's wildlife is found nowhere else. Best free ride in animal history.
A San Jose woman named Rebecca Morgan started handing out books to trick-or-treaters in 1995 because she didn't like that candy was the main treat. Somewhere a kid is still waiting for the Snickers.
Before pumpkins, people in Ireland and Britain carved turnips, and the jack-o'-lantern grew out of the story of Stingy Jack. Pumpkins are just the easier upgrade.
Candy maker William W. Kolb made an early candy apple in Newark, New Jersey, in 1908 while experimenting with red cinnamon-flavored candy. An experiment gone deliciously right.
Some believe knock-knock jokes came from Middle Ages guards using call-and-answer routines to identify people arriving at the castle after dark. "Who's there?" used to be a security question.
Trick-or-treating for UNICEF began in Philadelphia in 1950, when kids collected coins in decorated milk cartons and raised $17. Not bad for a carton of coins.
It's a day for adults handing out candy to sneak some for themselves before the kids start knocking. The bowl is always lighter than you bought.
The Halloween & Costume Association created it in 2019 after a petition to move Halloween to the last Saturday in October. Compromise: more candy, same date.
Daylight saving time ends today, and author Nancy Christie says to spend the extra hour taking a breath instead of doing more work. The kids will not have read this.
It's a day to stop thinking about the things you "should" do, like exercising, eating healthier or getting organized. The laundry never got the memo.
"Calzone" translates to "trousers" or "pants legs," and the folded pizza started in Naples as street food for workers. So technically you're eating pants.
In 1884, 25 nations met in Washington to pick the Prime Meridian, and 22 voted for Greenwich while Haiti voted no and Brazil and France abstained. Somebody always wants to be different.
McCormick created it in 2019 to kick off what it calls #CinnamonSeason. Even the spice rack has a hashtag.
The Vegan Society picked it because the group's exact founding date in 1944 wasn't known. When in doubt, pick the first of the month.
Vinegar takes anywhere from a few months to a year to ferment. Patience, it's sour.
Nellie Verne Burt McPherson, an Illinois women's club president, started it in 1928 to thank her favorite author, Irving Bacheller. The original fan mail.
It honors radio and TV traffic departments and marks the first commercial radio broadcast, on Pittsburgh's KDKA in 1920, which happened to be election night. Hope someone logged it correctly.
Jim Henson's Cookie Monster debuted on Sesame Street in 1969 after starting in 1966 as a "Wheel-Stealer." Honestly, relatable.
Deviled eggs are also called eggs mimosa, stuffed eggs and dressed eggs. Potluck's fastest vanishing act.
It's a day for kids learning shapes to look up, down and every which way to point out circles. Kids will find a circle everywhere.
John Montagu, the fourth Earl of Sandwich, was born in 1718, and legend says he came up with the sandwich in 1762. He also served as Postmaster General, so he delivered mail and lunch.
Jellyfish are about 95 percent water, and a lion's mane jellyfish can weigh over 440 pounds. Basically a water balloon with opinions.
People use as many cliché phrases as they can today, even though those phrases were once fresh and novel. It's the same old story.
Adrienne Sioux Koopersmith created it in 1996, and it's held on every Friday the 13th and on Election Day. Doubt everything, even this fact.
King Tut took the throne at age nine, and Howard Carter found his tomb in 1922. Most nine-year-olds can't even clean their rooms.
Kenner introduced the Easy-Bake Oven in 1963, and the original cooked with ordinary light bulbs. Talk about a bright idea.
Candy starts with sugar dissolved in water, and the hotter the water gets, the more sugar dissolves. Science class, now with a sweet tooth.
It has been observed every year since 2007. Pretty common name for something so rare.
